english.title: Import a drug of a temporary class to which a prohibition applies
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were concerned in the importation of goods, namely **(..SPECIFY THE QUANTITY AND TYPE OF DRUG..), which were subject to a temporary class drug order, contrary to a prohibition in force by virtue of **(..SPECIFY THE ENACTMENT..) and with intent to evade the prohibition imposed by section 3(1) of the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971
english.legislation: Contrary to section 50(3), (4), (5) and Schedule 1 of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.

english.notes:
(i) Section 50(5) states: In the case of an offence under subsection (2) or (3) above in connection with a prohibition or restriction on importation having effect by virtue of section 3 of the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971, subsection (4) above shall have effect subject to the modifications specified in Schedule 1 to this Act.
(ii) Paragraph 1 of Schedule 1 states:1 Sections 50(4), 68(3), and 170(3) of this Act shall have effect in a case where the goods in respect of which the offence referred to in that subsection was committed were a Class A drug, Class B drug or a temporary class drug as if for the words from "shall be liable" onwards there were substituted the following words, that is to say -"shall be liable -(a) on summary conviction, to a penalty of £20,000 or of three times the value of the goods, whichever is the greater, or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 6 months, or to both;
(b) on conviction on indictment -(i) where the goods were a Class A drug, to a penalty of any amount, or to imprisonment for life, or to both; and (ii) where they were a Class B drug or a temporary class drug, to a penalty of any amount, or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 14 years, or to both".

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine of £20,000 or of three times the value of the goods, whichever is the greater.
Indictment: maximum 14 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see see section 282(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.
